content: 1. A study published in 2011 in the journal Infectious Diseases in Obstetrics and Gynecology examined sexually transmitted infections (STIs) among female sex workers in two cities in India. 2. Steen, Cherisch, and de Vlas (2012) discussed the implementation of periodic presumptive treatment for curable STIs among sex workers in Current Opinion in Infectious Diseases. 3. Denison et al. (2008) conducted a meta-analysis on the impact of HIV voluntary counseling and testing, as well as behavioral risk reduction, in developing countries between 1990 and 2005, published in AIDS and Behavior. 4. The World Health Organization (WHO) released guidance in 2007 on provider-initiated HIV testing and counseling in healthcare facilities, emphasizing its importance in early detection and management. 5. In 2010, WHO provided recommendations on delivering HIV test results, re-testing, and counseling for adults, highlighting the need for effective communication strategies. 6. WHO's 2012 guidance focused on HIV testing and counseling for couples, including antiretroviral therapy for treatment and prevention in serodiscordant couples. 7. Jacobson et al. (2002) evaluated the effectiveness of highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) in HIV patients by using biomarkers to assess disease progression, as published in the American Journal of Epidemiology. 8. Farmer et al. (2001) explored community-based approaches to HIV treatment in resource-poor settings, emphasizing the importance of local engagement, as reported in The Lancet. 9. Kasper et al. (2003) demystified antiretroviral therapy in resource-limited settings, providing practical insights in the Essential Drugs Monitor. 10. Attawell and Mundy (2003) reviewed the provision of antiretroviral therapy in resource-limited settings, summarizing experiences up to August 2003 in a report for the UK Department for International Development. 11. WHO's 2011 report on the global HIV/AIDS response provided an update on the epidemic and progress toward universal access to prevention, treatment, and care. 12. Mills et al. (2006) conducted a systematic review of barriers and facilitators to HAART adherence in developed and developing nations, published in PLoS Medicine. 13. Huet et al. (2011) examined long-term virological, immunological, and mortality outcomes in HIV-infected female sex workers treated with HAART in Africa, as reported in BMC Public Health. 14. Cohen et al. (2011) demonstrated the effectiveness of early antiretroviral therapy in preventing HIV-1 infection, as published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 15. WHO's 2010 guidelines for antiretroviral therapy in adults and adolescents provided evidence-based recommendations for treatment strategies. 16. Chen et al. (2005) studied the prevalence of STIs among female sex workers in Yunnan, China, as reported in AIDS Patient Care and STDs. 17. Sethi et al. (2006) analyzed HIV, STIs, and risk behaviors among male sex workers in London over a 10-year period, as published in Sexually Transmitted Infections. 18. Todd et al. (2006) investigated the prevalence and correlates of HIV infection among female sex workers in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, as reported in Sexually Transmitted Diseases. 19. Tran et al. (2005) studied HIV infection and risk characteristics among female sex workers in Hanoi, Vietnam, as published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 20. Verster et al. (2001) examined the prevalence of HIV infection and risk behaviors among street prostitutes in Rome between 1997 and 1998, as reported in AIDS Care. 21. The Monitoring the AIDS Pandemic (MAP) Network released a 2005 report on sex work and HIV/AIDS in Asia, providing regional insights into the epidemic. 22. WHO's 2004 technical paper highlighted the effectiveness of sterile needle and syringe programs in reducing HIV/AIDS among injecting drug users. 23. WHO, UNODC, and UNAIDS published a 2012 technical guide for countries to set targets for universal access to HIV prevention, treatment, and care for injecting drug users. 24. Lee (1997) provided a comprehensive review of hepatitis B virus infection in the New England Journal of Medicine. 25. Lemon, Lok, and Alter (2008) discussed viral hepatitis in the context of sexually transmitted diseases in a McGraw-Hill publication. 26. Todd et al. (2010) reported on the prevalence of HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C among female sex workers in three Afghan cities, as published in AIDS. 27. Nuttbrock et al. (2009) examined lifetime risk factors for HIV and STIs among male-to-female transgender individuals, as reported in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 28. Nguyen et al. (2011) studied the prevalence of hepatitis B virus infection among different HIV-risk groups in Hai Phong, Vietnam, as published in the Journal of Medical Virology. 29. Dos Ramos Farias et al. (2011) provided the first report on STIs among transgender and male sex workers in Argentina, highlighting high prevalence rates of HIV, HPV, HBV, and syphilis, as published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases. 30. Lai et al. (2003) reviewed hepatitis B in The Lancet, providing insights into its global impact and management. 31. WHO's 2009 position paper on hepatitis B outlined strategies for prevention and control, as published in the Weekly Epidemiological Record. 32. WHO's 2012 guidance addressed the prevention of viral hepatitis among people who inject drugs, emphasizing harm reduction strategies. 33. Geibel et al. (2011) evaluated the impact of peer outreach on HIV knowledge and prevention behaviors among male sex workers in Mombasa, Kenya. 34. Vuylsteke et al. (2004) assessed the quality of STI services for female sex workers in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, as reported in Tropical Medicine and International Health. 35. Nyamuryekung’e et al. (1997) evaluated acceptable approaches to providing STD services for women at truck stops in Tanzania, as published in the East African Medical Journal. 36. Heiligenberg et al. (2012) reported a high prevalence of STIs among HIV-infected men during routine outpatient visits in the Netherlands, as published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases. 37. The Global Commission on HIV and the Law (2012) released a report titled Risks, Rights & Health, addressing the intersection of HIV, human rights, and legal frameworks.
